resource.description: Who really pays your x402 endpoint. For a Base payTo address: every USDC payer in the last 30 days labelled probe (directory probe or test-buy wallet, 164-wallet list), self (funded by the payTo or a wallet it funded), fleet (one funder sent the same amount to 3+ payers), real (3+ payments on 2+ days) or once; with tx count, USD, funders, settling facilitator, CDP/PayAI listing status and suggestions. A payTo not in the data set is a free 404. Data rebuilt offline from Base RPC. Labels are rule-based classifications of public transfers, not allegations; they can be wrong (refunds, promotional credits).

example.disclaimer: Labels are rule-based classifications of public on-chain USDC transfers. They describe funding and payment patterns, not intent, and are not an allegation of wash trading or any wrongdoing by a seller or payer. They can be wrong (for example refunds or promotional credits sent by a seller make its customers look self-funded). Corrections: https://github.com/walkley/x402-content-site/issues
suggestions: 1 of 2 payers are directory probes and test-buy wallets ($0.006). Do not count them as users; they pay once per new route to check delivery.

1 payers ($0.01) are labelled self: they received USDC from this payTo or from a wallet it funded. If those transfers were not refunds or credits to customers, leave these payers out of revenue and listing metrics.
No payer paid on 2 or more days with 3 or more payments. Repeat use is the signal to watch; directory listing alone has not produced it.
Not in the CDP Bazaar snapshot. CDP lists a route after the CDP facilitator settles a payment for it; most sampled agent payments on Base are settled by CDP.
Not in the PayAI directory snapshot. PayAI lists a route after it settles one payment for it (a self-payment works).
All revenue in the window came from payers labelled probe, self or fleet.
